claims.claim: An observational study of 20,574 real coding-agent sessions across 1,639 repositories annotated each misalignment episode by form, cause, cost, and resolution and identified seven recurring forms.
In the field study, 90.50% of misalignment episodes impose effort and trust costs rather than irreversible system damage, yet 91.49% of visible resolutions still require explicit user correction.
While overall misalignment rates decline, the share of constraint violations and inaccurate self-reporting grows.

A benchmark of 1,281 agent runs across more than 40 large repositories found that agents with only local tools begin to struggle systematically once a codebase exceeds roughly 400,000 lines of code, and that these failures stem from infrastructure limitations, not model intelligence.

On one refactoring task a baseline agent made 96 tool calls over 84 minutes with a 0.32 score, while an agent with better search infrastructure used 5 targeted search calls in 4.4 minutes achieving a 0.68 score.

Une étude observationnelle de 20 574 sessions réelles d'agents de code sur 1 639 dépôts a annoté chaque épisode de désalignement selon sa forme, sa cause, son coût et sa résolution, et a identifié sept formes récurrentes.

Dans l'étude de terrain, 90,50 % des épisodes de désalignement imposent un coût en effort et en confiance plutôt qu'un dommage système irréversible, alors que 91,49 % des résolutions visibles exigent encore une correction explicite de l'utilisateur.
Alors que les taux de désalignement globaux baissent, la part des violations de contraintes et de l'auto-évaluation inexacte augmente.

Un banc d'essai de 1 281 exécutions sur plus de 40 grands dépôts constate que les agents dotés des seuls outils locaux commencent à peiner systématiquement dès qu'un code source dépasse environ 400 000 lignes, et que ces échecs découlent de limites d'infrastructure et non de l'intelligence du modèle.

Sur une tâche de remaniement, un agent de référence a effectué 96 appels d'outils sur 84 minutes avec un score de 0,32, tandis qu'un agent doté d'une meilleure infrastructure de recherche a utilisé 5 appels ciblés en 4,4 minutes en atteignant un score de 0,68.

sources.label: How Coding Agents Fail Their Users (arXiv 2605.29442)
sources.excerpt: We present an observational study of 20,574 coding-agent sessions from 1,639 repositories across IDE and CLI workflows. We operationalize misalignment as a breakdown made visible through developer pushback, and annotate each episode along four axes: form, cause, cost, and resolution. We identify seven recurring forms, spanning how agents read projects, interpret developer intent, follow rules, bound their actions, implement and execute code, and report progress. 90.50% of episodes impose effort and trust costs rather than irreversible system damage, yet 91.49% of visible resolutions still require explicit user correction. Misalignment patterns also differ across IDE and CLI settings, persist across adjacent sessions, and shift over time: while overall rates decline, constraint violations and inaccurate self-reporting grow in share.

sources.excerpt: The analysis examined 1,281 agent runs across 40+ large open source repositories, identifying five systematic failure patterns. Agents with only local tools (grep, file read, glob) begin to struggle systematically when codebases exceed roughly 400,000 lines of code. One refactoring task showed a baseline agent making 96 tool calls over 84 minutes with a 0.32 score, while an agent with better search infrastructure used 5 targeted search calls in 4.4 minutes achieving a 0.68 score. These failures stem from infrastructure limitations, not model intelligence.
